basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 9.' and it opens 'Vers. 9. Ludentem. Tradunt Hebraei quod idola | fecerit quasi ludens quibus infantiam'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 9. Ludentem. Tradunt Hebraei quod idola | fecerit quasi ludens quibus infantiam Isaac deciperet. Beatus quoque Hieronymus dicit quod quasi major per ludum primogenita sibi praesumpserit. Absolute autem possumus dicere quod eum lubricum et lascivum facere volebat, sicut ipse erat. Unde et Apostolus hunc ludum persecutionem appellat dicens: Sed, tunc sicut is qui secundum carnem natus est persequebatur eum qui secundum spiritum, ita et nunc (Gal. IV, 29).
